item.title: Beauty Is All That Matters: Duck Typing and Protocols
item.description:
The question arises: treat a thing based on what it does, or based on what it is?

Python was always clear on this. “If it quacks like a duck, treat it like a duck." You don’t ask an object for its pedigree, you ask it to quack.

This comes with a consequence: you don’t find out until you try. You usually don’t discover incompatibilities until some code actually tries to use the expected interface. And you rarely get to walk every path. It’s error-prone, slow, tiring, and worse than a mandatory two-hour synergy meeting. For big, important projects, “run it and see what explodes” is not a plan (done it with my life).

item.title: Some good bad advice
item.description: Between watching the new Spider-Noir and upsetting myself with the June 7th election drama in my country, I opted for a third option: writing this article. Truth be told, looking at the political landscape back home, it’s hard not to get some popcorn, shut off your brain, put on the hat of a football fan, and watch some fruitless debates. I almost regret not capitalizing on those heavily subsidized diaspora flights just to go back and vote; there really is nothing quite like the irony of people deciding the fate of a country without having to bear any of the daily consequences.
